chunks.h: When package-managed is the right choice
chunks.t:
- Tests. You can mock the application clock for deterministic timestamps.
- Single-writer apps. Every write goes through the package, so coverage isn't an issue.
- Time zone handling is the app's job. You've already wrapped your DB driver to use UTC.

chunks.h: When DB-managed is the right choice (default recommendation)
chunks.t:
- Multiple writers. Other services, scripts, manual SQL.
- Multi-region / replicated databases. You want a single clock source.
- Production. Give the database the last word on time.

Use executeSqlTransaction() to span multiple service calls in one atomic unit.

For operations that span multiple services (or multiple calls to the same service), the package exposes executeSqlTransaction() for explicit transaction control.
executeSqlTransaction opens a transaction on the configured database, runs the callback, commits on success, and rolls back on any thrown error.

Every CRUD method accepts an optional last argument of SqlOperationOptions. Pass { transaction: tx } to enlist the call in an existing transaction:

The tx handle is a Drizzle transaction object. It's typed as any in
SqlOperationOptions so the package doesn't depend on a specific
Drizzle transaction type. Pass it through to other Drizzle calls if you
need to drop down to raw queries inside the transaction.

chunks.h: Mixing package methods with raw Drizzle
chunks.t: The tx is the standard Drizzle transaction handle. Anything you can do with db you can do with tx, and it'll be enlisted in the same transaction.

executeSqlTransaction can be nested in code, but each call opens its own savepoint. If an inner callback throws, the outer transaction is unaffected. For most use cases, prefer a single top-level executeSqlTransaction per request.

Failure Behavior 
--- --- 
The callback throws The transaction is rolled back. The error propagates to the caller. 
A nested massCreate throws BulkOperationException The transaction is rolled back. The exception propagates. 
The connection drops mid-transaction The database rolls back. The package surfaces the underlying error.

- Cross-service atomicity. Creating a User and a Profile in one atomic unit.
- Read-modify-write consistency. Read a row, decide based on its value, write back, all in one transaction.
- Bulk operations that need external side effects in the same atomic unit. See Bulk operations (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations).

- Read-only queries, findAll, count, findOne don't need a transaction.
- Independent writes. If the operations can fail or succeed independently, separate transactions are usually better (smaller blast radius on failure).
- Long-running operations. Transactions hold locks. Don't include network calls, queue publishes, or unbounded awaits inside a transaction.

- → Bulk operations: transactional by default, but executeSqlTransaction is for cross-service work (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations)
- → Lifecycle hooks, before / after fire on every CRUD call, including those inside transactions (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/hooks-validation)

upsert and massUpsert insert a row or update the one that already holds its unique key, in one statement: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on Postgres, ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE on MySQL.

upsert(dto, { conflictTarget, update }) inserts the row, or updates the existing row that already has the same unique key, in one statement. It returns the row as stored either way.

On Postgres this is INSERT... ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = excluded.name, role = excluded.role,... RETURNING.

Field Default Notes 
--- --- --- 
conflictTarget the primary key A column or a list of columns with a unique constraint or index. An unknown column is a 400. 
update every column you sent, except the conflict target, the primary key and createdAt The columns to overwrite when the row exists. updatedAt is included, so it moves on an update. 

Pass update: [] to keep the existing row untouched. The row still comes back, which makes upsert a get-or-create:

c.s: const tag = await tags.upsert({ name: 'urgent' }, { conflictTarget: 'name', update: [] });

chunks.t: validateCreate, beforeCreate and mapCreateDtoToEntity, because the statement starts as an insert, and writableColumns (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/allowlists) applies. The after hooks do not run, since the package cannot tell an insert from an update without an extra query.

chunks.h: Does upsert work with scope, versions and relations?
chunks.t: Yes. On a scoped entity (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/multi-tenancy) the scope is written onto the row and sits in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE... WHERE, so a conflict with another tenant's row updates nothing and is a 404 (a 400 on MySQL, which has no such WHERE). The scope and version (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/optimistic-locking) columns are never overwritten from the body; the version goes up by one when the row already existed. options.relations and options.counts load onto the returned row, and the upsert events (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/events) fire when global hooks are on.
The same mapping as create. A unique violation on a different key is a 409, a value the column cannot hold is a 400, and a foreign key that points nowhere is a 400.

c.s:
// sku is unique too: moving row 1 onto row 2's sku is a 409
await items.upsert({ id: 1, sku: 'A2', ... }, { conflictTarget: 'id' });

chunks.t: massUpsert(rows, upsertOptions, options?) is one INSERT... ON CONFLICT for the whole batch, in a transaction. When it fails, the failing items are named in a BulkOperationException (https://crud.avytrix.dev/docs/bulk-operations#what-does-a-failed-bulk-call-return-over-http). Two rows of the same batch with the same conflict key are a 400 on Postgres ("the same key appears more than once in one upsert"), because one statement cannot update a row twice.

MySQL uses ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, which fires on any unique key, so conflictTarget does not choose the key there. MySQL has no RETURNING either, so the package reads the rows back by conflictTarget: send a value for every conflict target column, otherwise it is a 400.
